70586-cutting-and-draping.title: Cutting And Draping
70586-cutting-and-draping.creator: Unknown
70586-cutting-and-draping.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. Figure I is an example of straight festoon drapery, the right side in skeleton to more clearly show the figures. To measure a door or window for this style it is necessary to have the extreme width of the space to be draped (5-0), the distance from the top of wood trim to floor (8-0) and the distance from the top of trim to ceiling (2-0).

arxiv-1912-10692.title: An Evolution Equation Approach to Linear Quantum Field Theory
arxiv-1912-10692.creator: Jan Dereziński and Daniel Siemssen
arxiv-1912-10692.description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by Jan Dereziński and Daniel Siemssen. In the first part of our paper we analyze (non-autonomous) pseudo-unitary evolutions on Krein spaces. We describe various bisolutions and inverses of the corresponding Cauchy data operator. We prove that with boundary conditions given by a maximal positive and maximal negative space we can always associate an inverse, which can be viewed as a generalization of the usual Feynman propagator . These constructions can be applied to a large class of globally hyperbolic manifolds.

arxiv-2009-04994.title: Correlations constrained by composite measurements
arxiv-2009-04994.creator: John H. Selby, Ana Belén Sainz, Victor Magron, Łukasz Czekaj, Michał Horodecki
arxiv-2009-04994.description: Abstract How to understand the set of correlations admissible in nature is one outstanding open problem in the core of the foundations of quantum theory. Here we take a complementary viewpoint to the device-independent approach, and explore the correlations that physical theories may feature when restricted by some particular constraints on their measurements.

arxiv-2104-05243.title: On Unifying Misinformation Detection
arxiv-2104-05243.creator: Nayeon Lee, Belinda Z. Li, Sinong Wang, Pascale Fung, Hao Ma, Wen-tau Yih, Madian Khabsa
arxiv-2104-05243.description: Abstract In this paper, we introduce UnifiedM2 , a general-purpose misinformation model that jointly models multiple domains of misinformation with a single, unified setup. The model is trained to handle four tasks: detecting news bias , clickbait , fake news and verifying rumors .

arxiv-2111-12454.title: Exploring Business Process Deviance with Sequential and Declarative Patterns Journal: Decision Support Systems
arxiv-2111-12454.creator: Giacomo Bergami, Chiara Di Francescomarino, Chiara Ghidini, Fabrizio Maria Maggi, Joonas Puura
arxiv-2111-12454.description: Abstract Business process deviance refers to the phenomenon whereby a subset of the executions of a business process deviate, in a negative or positive way, with respect to their expected or desirable outcomes. Deviant executions of a business process include those that violate compliance rules, or executions that undershoot or exceed performance targets.

arxiv-2111-15266.title: Two-stage Temporal Modelling Framework for Video-based Depression Recognition using Graph Representation
arxiv-2111-15266.creator: Jiaqi Xu, Siyang Song, Keerthy Kusumam, Hatice Gunes, Michel Valstar
arxiv-2111-15266.description: Abstract Video-based automatic depression analysis provides a fast, objective and repeatable self-assessment solution, which has been widely developed in recent years. While depression clues may be reflected by human facial behaviours of various temporal scales, most existing approaches either focused on modelling depression from short-term or video-level facial behaviours.

arxiv-2208-08711.title: L3: Accelerator-Friendly Lossless Image Format for High-Resolution, High-Throughput DNN Training
arxiv-2208-08711.creator: Jonghyun Bae, Woohyeon Baek, Tae Jun Ham, Jae W. Lee
arxiv-2208-08711.description: Abstract The training process of deep neural networks (DNNs) is usually pipelined with stages for data preparation on CPUs followed by gradient computation on accelerators like GPUs. In an ideal pipeline, the end-to-end training throughput is eventually limited by the throughput of the accelerator, not by that of data preparation.

arxiv-2504-14270.title: Convergence Laws for Extensions of First-Order Logic with Averaging
arxiv-2504-14270.creator: Sam Adam-Day, Michael Benedikt, Alberto Larrauri
arxiv-2504-14270.description: Abstract . For many standard models of random structure, first-order logic sentences exhibit a convergence phenomenon on random inputs. The most well-known example is for random graphs with constant edge probability, where the probabilities of first-order sentences converge to 0 or 1.

arxiv-2507-17470.title: Demonstration of Efficient Predictive Surrogates for Large-scale Quantum Processors
arxiv-2507-17470.creator: Wei-You Liao 1, Yuxuan Du 2,∗, Xinbiao Wang 2, Tian-Ci Tian 1, Yong Luo 3, Bo Du 3, Dacheng Tao 2, He-Liang Huang 1
arxiv-2507-17470.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Wei-You Liao 1, Yuxuan Du 2,∗, Xinbiao Wang 2, Tian-Ci Tian 1, Yong Luo 3, Bo Du 3, Dacheng Tao 2, He-Liang Huang 1. The ongoing development of quantum processors is driving breakthroughs in scientific discovery. Despite this progress, the formidable cost of fabricating large-scale quantum processors means they will remain rare for the foreseeable future, limiting their widespread application.

europmc-pmc3531506.title: PRIME: a programme to reduce the treatment gap for mental disorders in five low- and middle-income countries.
europmc-pmc3531506.creator: Lund C, Tomlinson M, De Silva M, Fekadu A, Shidhaye R, Jordans M, Petersen I, Bhana A, Kigozi F, Prince M, Thornicroft G, Hanlon C, Kakuma R, McDaid D, Saxena S, Chisholm D, Raja S, Kippen-Wood S, Honikman S, Fairall L, Patel V.

pmc-10736348.title: EXPLORATORY FACTOR ANALYSIS OF THE COMFORT ASSESSMENT IN DYING WITH DEMENTIA SCALE
pmc-10736348.creator: Peiyuan Zhang, Timothy Stump, Wanzhu Tu, Todd Becker, Jessica Orth, Alexander Floyd, Kathleen Unroe, John Cagle
pmc-10736348.description: The 14-item Comfort Assessment in Dying with Dementia (CAD-EOLD) scale is a widely used instrument measuring end-of-life care for people with dementia (PWD). The instrument has been used to evaluate symptom burden among PWD in nursing homes, but the measurement properties are less studied for symptoms reported by family and staff caregivers.

pmc-11381541.title: An open-source tool for automated human-level circling behavior detection
pmc-11381541.creator: O. R. Stanley, A. Swaminathan, E. Wojahn, C. Bao, Z. M. Ahmed, K. E. Cullen
pmc-11381541.description: Quantitatively relating behavior to underlying biology is crucial in life science. Although progress in keypoint tracking tools has reduced barriers to recording postural data, identifying specific behaviors from this data remains challenging. Manual behavior coding is labor-intensive and inconsistent, while automatic methods struggle to explicitly define complex behaviors, even when they seem obvious to the human eye.

pmc-11433996.title: Profoxydim in Focus: A Structural Examination of Herbicide Behavior in Gas and Aqueous Phases
pmc-11433996.creator: María Cobos-Escudero, Paula Pla, Álvaro Cervantes-Diaz, José Luis Alonso-Prados, Pilar Sandín-España, Manuel Alcamí, Al Mokhtar Lamsabhi
pmc-11433996.description: This study investigates the chemical structure of profoxydim, focusing on its E–isomer, the main commercial form. The research aimed to determine the predominant tautomeric forms under various environmental conditions. Using proton and carbon–13 NMR spectroscopy alongside theoretical modeling, we examined tautomers and their conformers in different solvents (MeOD, DMSO, CDCl3, benzene) to mimic gas and aqueous phases.

pmc-11545183.title: The Effect of Motivators and Barriers on Attitudes and Willingness to Consume Dairy Functional Foods in Hungary
pmc-11545183.creator: Mohammad Mohammad, Isaac Hyeladi Malgwi, Stefano Schiavon, Orsolya Szigeti, Witoon Prinyawiwatkul, Raquel P F Guiné, Maria Ewa Rembiałkowska
pmc-11545183.description: As the global trend for healthy eating grows, firms are emphasising dairy functional foods (DFFs). This study looks into the relationship between consumer attitudes and readiness to consume DFFs, taking into account how a healthy lifestyle might both motivate and deter people from using them.

pmc-12032466.title: Automated High-Throughput Live Cell Monitoring of Scratch Wound Closure
pmc-12032466.creator: Kevin Schmidt, Dominik Lerm, Arne Schmidt, Nicholas Dickel, Jan Fiedler, Thomas Thum, Meik Kunz
pmc-12032466.description: Background:Angiogenesis and regenerative wound healing rely on the promotion of distinct endothelial cell phenotypes exhibiting increased migratory capacity. Monitoring of these hallmark events in vitro is invaluable for discovering novel therapeutics. However, respective methods often lack a high-throughput character or accurate analysis tools, which are essential for effective screening suitability.

pmc-12615791.title: Using machine learning to predict student outcomes for early intervention and formative assessment
pmc-12615791.creator: Bilal Baris Alkan, Serafettin Kuzucuk, Nesrin Alkan, Alper Sinan
pmc-12615791.description: The increasing importance of early prediction of student performance has led to research into machine learning models that can be used to assess student outcomes more accurately.This study focused on developing a predictive model based on machine learning algorithms to evaluate student performance and provide early intervention mechanisms.

pmc-13324887.creator: Kari Hemminki, Frantisek Zitricky, Asta Försti, Akseli Hemminki
pmc-13324887.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Similar positive news have also been announced from the UK (Cancer in the UK: Overview 2024) [2, 3]. The Nordic countries with high-level national cancer registries also witnessed a positive development of cancer survival [4, 5].

pmc-13569464.title: Alcohol abstinence precipitates alcohol seeking and aversion-resistant intake in association with increased BNST activity
pmc-13569464.creator: Marie A. Doyle, Hye Jean Yoon, Megan E. Altemus, Anika S. Park, Martha E. Troutman, Laura Grunenkovaite, Danielle N. Adank, Caitlyn M. Edwards, Nia A. Chetkovich, Sabrina D. Hallal, Louise Lantier, Cody A. Siciliano, Erin S. Calipari, Danny G. Winder
pmc-13569464.description: Alcohol Use Disorder (AUD) is defined by a common diagnostic framework, yet individuals show diverse drinking patterns and relapse vulnerabilities during abstinence, reflecting neurobiological heterogeneity. The bed nucleus of the stria terminalis (BNST) is well positioned to contribute to this variability.
